results.title: It's a crime
results.creator_credit: Wolf Koenig, Tom Daly and ONF | NFB
results.brief_description: An animated film, in a humorous vein, showing how seasonal unemployment may be greatly lessened if industry, and the public generally, avail themselves of the increased labor supply during winter lay-offs. The advice comes from someone who knows—a gentleman thief and safecracker whose nefarious but highly skilled profession gives him a particular advantage in assessing the state of business, and the contents of strong boxes, during the winter fall-off of work. How the situation may be rectified with a little foresight and imagination is amply and amusingly illustrated. Animation by Gerald Potterton and commentary by Guy Glover.

results.title: It's a business doing pleasure
results.creator_credit: Sharon Connolly, John Moore and Open Channel Productions
results.brief_description: An intelligent look at prostitution, focusing on sex workers, Vicky and Gillian, two of the thousands of women working in the sex industry in Victoria. They work in one of Melbourne’s legal brothels and give a detailed explanation of the practicality of their work, of which sex is only one component. Vicky and Gillian earn more than women in low skill jobs, but experience none of the benefits of other wage earners. Also covers the work of the Prostitutes’ Collective of Victoria.

results.title: Issues in psychology
results.creator_credit: Harry Ratner, David Stone and Coastline Community College
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “Psychology: the study of human behavior”.
Psychology is a dynamic, diverse discipline concerned with the study of the human condition. What are the major issues in, and impact of, psychology today? To examine this question, a panel of US psychologists are assembled including psychobiologist, James McGaugh, social psychologist, Lee Ross, cognitive/social psychologist, Elizabeth Loftus, and Professor Joseph White, a developmental psychologist.

results.title: Issues in education: the Chief Executive - schooling P-12
results.creator_credit: Trevor Lunn and Victoria. Schools Division. Curriculum Branch
results.brief_description: Dr. Graham Allen, Chief Executive, Ministry of Education, explains Victoria’s school curriculum plan for preparatory level to Year 12. The objective is to have the maximum number of students completing Year 12. The curriculum includes a broad education spectrum up to Year 10, with specialized subjects during Years 11-12, enabling astudents to pursue further education or to join the workforce with a knowledge of current technology.

results.title: Israeli boy: life on a kibbutz
results.creator_credit: Ruth Broyde and Encyclopaedia Britannica Films
results.brief_description: Differing in their degree of adherence to pioneer customs, in their size, in what they produce and in the philosophy that unites each membership, the kibbutzim of Israel are greatly diverse. Here, a young Israeli boy describes life as it is on his particular kibbutz where the children are raised apart from their parents but retain close family ties. Nir explains how his kibbutz operates and tells about his family’s role on the kibbutz.

results.title: Israel: an adventure
results.creator_credit: Alexander Hammid, Franta G. Herman, Nathan Kroll and Israel Government Tourist Office
results.brief_description: A kaleidoscopic tour of Israel where the past, present and future lie open side by side: Acre, where Jew and Arab work peacefully side by side; the modern city of Haifa with its harbour, industries and big blocks of flats; the Catacombs, Hebrew University; Jerusalem with its churches from many countries and a Yemenite wedding rehearsal. Narrated by Christopher Plummer.
